Consult Summary:
45-year-old female hotel housekeeper with 3–4 months of painful, itchy, cracked palmar skin—worsened over the last week—consistent with occupational contact dermatitis. Plan includes topical steroid, regular emollient use, strict glove protection, and review in 10–14 days.

Problem List:

Issue 1: Suspected contact irritant dermatitis of palms
- Onset 3–4 months ago after starting new housekeeping job; progressively worse, now limiting work (absent past 3 days).
- Symptoms: pain, dryness, cracking, intermittent itching; occasional bleeding only after scratching.
- No systemic symptoms (no fever, nausea, vomiting, bowel or urinary issues).
- Likely trigger: cleaning chemicals without gloves.
- Tried OTC E45 cream and an antihistamine – no relief.
- Impression: Occupational contact dermatitis vs. irritant eczema.
- Management: Prescribed topical steroid cream (name/dose/route/frequency not documented) + “stronger emollients” to be applied 3–4 times/day x 2 weeks; strict glove use; review if no improvement or worsening within 10–14 days.

Issue 2: Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus
- Patient-reported diagnosis; no details on duration or control.
- Medication: Metformin (dose/route/frequency not documented).
- No acute diabetic complaints today.

Issue 3: Generalized mild dry skin on legs
- Long-standing, not severe; mentioned during review of systems.
- No current treatment required; may benefit from general skin hydration advice.

Medications:
- Metformin – dose/route/frequency not documented.
- OTC E45 emollient cream – patient-initiated.
- OTC antihistamine – patient-initiated, ineffective.

Allergies:
- No known drug or other allergies reported.

Past Medical History:
- Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus.
- No history of eczema, dermatitis, asthma, or bowel disease.

Social History:
- Occupation: Hotel housekeeper; frequent exposure to cleaning agents, inconsistent glove use.
- Smoking: Non-smoker.
- Alcohol: “A couple of pints” once per week (low intake).

Preventative History:
- Not discussed (cervical screening, vaccinations, etc. not documented).

Physical Examination:
- Conducted via telehealth; no vitals or physical findings documented.

Plan:
- Prescribe topical steroid cream (Rx sent to pharmacy).
- Prescribe/advise use of high-strength emollient; apply 3–4 times daily.
- Strict glove use during all cleaning tasks to avoid chemical exposure.
- Follow-up: Return if symptoms worsen or fail to improve within 10–14 days.
- Consider alternative therapies or referral to dermatology if no response.
